#5561. Teleport makes Beams generally available to bring AI agents into production

Infrastructure identity company Teleport today made Teleport Beams, its runtime for artificial intelligence agents that work on production infrastructure, generally available.

Beams goes after what Teleport sees as the main reason agents have stayed out of production so far. Most enterprises have not plugged agents into those systems at all, according to Ev Kontsevoy, Teleport’s co-founder and chief executive. He blamed gaps such as delegated identity and an audit trail that follows an agent from intent to action.

Sandboxes, the tool many teams reach for now, mostly isolate the agent in a virtual machine and handle its credentials. “When the cost of an error is high, traditional sandboxes don’t cut it,” Kontsevoy said ahead of the announcement.

Teleport calls each individual runtime a Beam, and every agent gets its own. A Beam carries a delegated identity inherited from the user or agent that launched it, while the agent inside starts with no standing privileges. Work begins with a proposed execution plan. That plan can be revised by a person or by a large language model acting as judge before a separate Beam runs it with only the approved roles. Reviewers then see new requests only for steps outside the plan.

Passwords never enter the agent’s environment. Everything the agent sends to a model is traced, and Teleport says that record lets Beams pick out a hijacked goal or agents coordinating in ways nobody planned. Each session also gets scored against the MITRE ATT&CK framework for a written risk summary. Seven of the detection rules come prebuilt, privilege escalation among them. Anything else a customer wants caught can be described in natural language and added to the set.

Each Beam is an ephemeral micro-VM on a virtualized network. Nothing gets in or out without passing Teleport’s controls, and the audit log keeps a copy of every protocol exchange. Snapshots taken by a feature named Phases carry the files and memory of an expiring Beam into the next one, so longer jobs do not have to start over.

Teams can also fork a Beam to try several approaches in parallel. When something goes badly wrong, a kill switch ends the agent’s activity and cuts all of its connections to production at once.

Teleport makes no promise about what a model will decide. A hijacked or mistaken agent inside a Beam can reach only what it was granted until its authority lapses at the end of the task, and every action it takes stays on the record.

Beams runs on top of the Teleport Infrastructure Identity Platform, which the company says is in production at more than 700 enterprises, Nasdaq Inc., DoorDash Inc. and Elastic N.V. among them. Cisco Systems Inc. became Teleport’s largest strategic investor in August.

Teleport first showed Beams in March, two months after publishing the Teleport Agentic Identity Framework that the runtime now puts into practice. Following a public beta, the product is available at beams.run.

#5560. Sorted Launches the All-in-One App for TCG Players and Collectors

The next evolution of TCG collection management, from Collectivus Holdings

LISBON, Portugal, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Collectivus Holdings, a leading distribution, consumer goods, and services company supporting retailers and brands across the trading card game and hobby industries, today announced the official launch of Sorted, a trading card game (TCG) collection management app built for players and collectors. Now out of beta, Sorted brings collection tracking, card valuation, deck building, and more into one intuitive app. It solves a problem every serious collector knows well: managing a growing collection across multiple games, platforms, and tools.

#5559. Nvidia and Jensen Huang sued by shareholders over alleged Chinese spy affair

Free daily briefing on global business news.

The class-action complaint seeks unspecified damages for investors who bought Nvidia stock between Oct. 9 and Nov. 8

David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Nvidia $NVDA and CEO Jensen Huang face a shareholder lawsuit alleging they misled investors regarding Huang's affair with a woman believed to be an agent of Chinese intelligence, according to The Associated Press.

The complaint, which retail investor Mark Kistenmacher submitted to a California court on Monday, alleges that the company and Jensen Huang never revealed the affair, according to The Associated Press. It also accuses them of making false statements about Nvidia's relationship with the company of Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the reports. The complaint says this posed a "material risk" to Nvidia's reputation and business prospects.

The suit is meant to cover all purchasers of Nvidia stock between Oct. 9, the day news of the affair surfaced, and Nov. 8, the day Nvidia announced it was looking into reports that Jensen Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort," according to The Associated Press. It demands a jury trial and damages in an amount it does not specify.

"As a result of Defendants' wrongful acts and omissions, and the precipitous decline in the market value of the Company's securities, Plaintiff and other Class members have suffered significant losses and damages," the complaint said, according to The Associated Press. It adds that investors would not have bought Nvidia stock at "artificially inflated prices" had they known the truth.

The suit was filed in federal court in San Jose, California, by the Rosen Law Firm, according to CBS News.

Nvidia stock fell $7.97 on Monday, erasing about $190 billion in market value. The stock was down before the opening bell on Tuesday.

Jensen Huang has acknowledged the affair and apologized, according to The Associated Press. He told Nvidia employees in a message released Sunday that he had been "unfaithful" to his wife, according to CBS News.

The New York Times reported that American intelligence agencies had concluded Alice Huang, a onetime executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, was collecting information on behalf of the Chinese government, according to The Associated Press. Megaspeed purchased Nvidia chips valued at over $4.8 billion during the last two years, according to The New York Times. The two Huangs are unrelated.

President Donald Trump said Monday that Jensen Huang told him he did not know the woman was an alleged spy. Trump said he believes Huang and that the FBI is reviewing the issue.

The Justice Department is conducting a criminal probe of Megaspeed, which is suspected of illegally funneling Nvidia AI chips to China. China's Foreign Ministry has called the allegation against Alice Huang unsubstantiated. Nvidia's board is conducting its own scrutiny of the affair.

S&P 500 futures barely budged Tuesday while market participants waited for October's CPI release, set for 8:30 a.m. ET.

Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 156 points, or 0.3%. Nasdaq $NDAQ-100 futures slipped 0.4%.

Economists polled by Dow Jones expect headline CPI to have risen 0.3% from the prior month and core CPI, which excludes food and energy costs, to have risen 0.2%, according to CNBC. In September, headline CPI climbed 0.6%, while the core reading rose 0.3%.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics will not provide annual figures in the report. The 2025 government shutdown prevented the agency from gathering certain information, so there is nothing to compare against.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a rate hike in December looks probable to him, and he did not rule out a bigger half-point move while price pressures remain stubborn. "While the precise timing of the hikes doesn't matter, ensuring that the promised hikes are implemented in a reasonable period of time does," Waller said, according to CNBC.

Traders see a quarter-point hike next month as all but certain, according to The Wall Street Journal. Waller's remarks pushed up Treasury yields.

Brent crude fell after President Donald Trump described renewed strikes on Iran as "quite unlikely."

In Europe, the pan-European Stoxx 600 was 0.6% higher. The U.K.’s FTSE 100 added 0.3%, France’s CAC 40 rose 0.9% and Germany’s DAX gained 0.9%.

In Asia, South Korea’s Kospi surged 4.3% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 added 2.9%. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index rose 0.4%, mainland China’s CSI 300 added 0.3% and Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 1.3%.

On Monday, the Dow gained 1,104 points, or 2.2%. The S&P 500 rose about 2.4% and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 2.7%. The rally followed a choppy week when investors fretted that construction of new data centers could slow after the Democrats' strong midterm showing, according to CNBC.

#5555. Commvault unveils Recovery Studio, AgentRecover update and joint work with three partners

Data protection provider Commvault Systems Inc. today used its SHIFT 2026 customer event to unveil Recovery Studio, a new service that will automate the rebuilding of entire business applications after an outage or cyberattack.

Four other announcements cover recovery for artificial intelligence agents and joint work with Databricks Inc., Nvidia Corp. and Zscaler Inc.

AgentRecover, the company’s tool for reversing damage done by AI agents, is being extended to agents built on Microsoft Corp.’s Foundry and on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore from Amazon Web Services Inc. Databricks and Nvidia technology will draw on governed enterprise data from Commvault’s Data Activate service. The Zscaler agreement is a strategic partnership centered on AI security.

Recovery Studio goes after the manual work of restoring a business one piece at a time. Data alone does not get an application running again. Without the identities, configurations and infrastructure it depends on, an application can stay offline long after its files are back.

A large enterprise may have hundreds of applications and thousands of identities to bring up in sequence. Getting back to even a minimal level of operation takes 28 days on average under conventional approaches, according to Commvault research from last year.

In place of that manual work, the service uses automated runbooks that rebuild and validate each component in order. Commvault said the runbooks also restore identity systems and cloud configurations, firewall rules included. Threat scans can run inside a runbook on supported resources, and the results feed into the call on whether a service is ready to go back into production. Operational, disaster and cyber recovery all run from the same platform.

Pranay Ahlawat, Commvault’s chief technology and AI officer, called the launch “the DevOps moment for recovery.” He said one orchestrated flow can take over from the spreadsheets and war rooms that recovery teams lean on today.

The AgentRecover update moves the company’s agent protection onto the platforms where businesses build production agents. In September Commvault added protection for agent configurations that tools such as Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code store on employee laptops.

Phil Goodwin, research vice president at International Data Corp., said conventional recovery assumes a discrete set of data at one point in time. Agents break that assumption, because the agent, its data and the resources around it all have to come back “at machine speed,” he said.

On Bedrock AgentCore and Foundry, the software discovers each agent and maps the data, applications and infrastructure it interacts with. If an agent goes rogue, its activity log shows which systems it may have touched across platforms.

Restores target the agent and whatever it changed. Customers can also run AgentRecover with Commvault’s identity recovery and change auditing tools to trace the identities an agent acted through.

The Databricks and Nvidia announcements both build on Data Activate, which turns backup copies protected by Commvault into datasets for analytics and AI. Much of the data companies hold is unstructured and scattered across systems. In research from BARC published by DataHub in June, 70% of data and AI leaders said less than half of their unstructured data could be found and used for AI.

Commvault Data Activate for Databricks shares data under Commvault management into Databricks through OpenSharing. The data arrives as governed tables in Unity Catalog with its ownership, access permissions and lineage intact.

Updates keep flowing as source content changes or is deleted, and customers do not have to rebuild a connection to every original source. Alan Atkinson, chief business development officer at Commvault, said the aim is “turning protected data into an active business asset.”

Nvidia’s part, delivered as a reference design for software-as-a-service and software deployments, centers on retrieval. Nvidia NIM microservices and Nemotron Retriever, together with the Nvidia cuVS library used with Apache Solr, extract and organize Commvault-protected content so applications and agents can pull from it more easily. Data Activate keeps that content current as source files change, retention periods expire or permissions are revoked.

On the security side, Commvault and Zscaler listed AI discovery, runtime governance and agent detection and recovery as early areas of collaboration, and the companies did not announce a joint product or availability date. Zscaler’s Security for AI line polices how employees and agents use AI tools. Dhawal Sharma, Zscaler’s executive vice president of AI security and strategic initiatives, said organizations need to be “prepared to recover quickly if something goes wrong.”

Recovery Studio, AgentRecover’s Amazon Bedrock AgentCore support and the Databricks integration are all due to enter early access in December, the last of them in select Microsoft Azure regions. Foundry support comes sooner, with early access targeted for this month.

The Nvidia reference design is set to reach general availability in 2027 after an early release in December. Recovery Studio will be priced on the amount of data configured for orchestrated recovery, and Commvault plans general availability in the coming months.

A virtual edition of SHIFT follows on Nov. 18.

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrueDialog, an enterprise platform for business texting, today announced the TrueDialog Model Context Protocol (MCP), a connector that lets people and AI agents send SMS and RCS messages and manage contacts from inside AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and others. The TrueDialog MCP is available in the ChatGPT Plugins directory, the Microsoft (Copilot) Connectors directory, and any assistant that supports MCP can connect through tdmcp.com.

As more business work moves into conversations with AI assistants, those assistants are only as useful as the actions they can take. An assistant can draft a customer text in seconds. Sending it to the right people, from a registered number, with opt-outs honored, still means leaving the assistant and logging in to a separate messaging platform. The gap is wider for teams that build agents into their own apps. The agent can decide whom to reach and what to say, yet it still needs a dependable, compliant way to send the text.

"AI assistants are becoming the place where work starts, and sending a customer text shouldn't be the step that pulls people out of it," said John Wright, CEO of TrueDialog. "The TrueDialog MCP gives our customers, and the agents they build, a direct line to their TrueDialog account, with the same delivery infrastructure and compliance protections behind every message."

MCP is the open standard AI assistants use to work with outside software. The TrueDialog MCP connects an assistant directly to a customer's TrueDialog account.

Business users in marketing, sales, customer service, and operations can put the TrueDialog MCP to work with prompts such as:

Developers decide which tools an agent may use (including read-only agents that cannot send), and every tool call and result comes back in the response so the app can store it or act on it. Paired with the TrueDialog API or custom AI workflows, marketers can create automated responses, scheduled campaigns, routing, and more.

AI built into how customers work with messaging

TrueDialog builds AI into the messaging workflow itself. The TrueDialog MCP joins the company's other purpose-built AI: TrueDeliveryÂ® for AI-powered deliverability, TrueOptOut for AI-powered opt-out intent detection, and AI Assistant in Comms Hub, which suggests replies. Together, they put people and their agents on one messaging platform.

The TrueDialog MCP runs on the same platform, with 100% U.S.-based customer service. TrueDialog is SOC 2 Type II, TX-RAMP, and ISO 9001 certified. The MCP is a new way into TrueDialog. Customers keep access to the full platform, native integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Microsoft Dynamics 365, and the API, all at standard TrueDialog pricing, with no added fee for the MCP.

The TrueDialog MCP is available now in the ChatGPT Plugins directory and the Microsoft (Copilot) Connectors directory. Emirates anticipates receiving only three to five Boeing $BA 777-9 jets next year, and that is the optimistic scenario, President Tim Clark said at a press event in Berlin on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg.

Emirates has purchased more of the 777-9, a reworked take on Boeing's 777 widebody, than any other airline. The airline forecast only a small number of the jets arriving in late 2027, with perhaps double that volume to follow a year later, according to Bloomberg.

Boeing said Monday it would trim part of the workforce at its commercial division. Clark called the move a "recognition" that Boeing cannot speed up output across its different programs as quickly as it hoped, and "therefore, it's pointless keeping people idle," according to Bloomberg.

Emirates requires the 777-9 as a successor for older jets, among them the Airbus A380, a model no longer being built. "As we move forward, we are desperately short of capacity," Clark said on Bloomberg Television. He said the supply chain "is not where it needs to be."

Clark is holding an order for 35 of the smaller Boeing 787 in reserve. He said he will decide within the next two months whether to follow through, depending on Boeing's progress with 777-9 handovers.

"If we decide to take them, I'm not sure Boeing would be able to deliver them to us until the early '30s," Clark said of the 787 models, according to Bloomberg. "They have such a logjam."

Boeing is eliminating 5% of the jobs in its commercial airplane unit as 737 Max production runs behind plan. The company has also had trouble raising 787 output from eight aircraft a month to 10.

The 777-9 has slipped by a minimum of six years from the date it was first meant to enter the market, according to Bloomberg. Deutsche Lufthansa, one of the jet's launch customers, is leaving it out of its plans for the summer timetable.

Infineon raised its fiscal 2027 forecast for data center revenue to close to €4 billion ($4.5 billion) as it reported fourth-quarter results on Tuesday. The German chipmaker said revenue from power supplies for data centers is projected to reach that level in the year ending in September 2027.

Infineon forecast total revenue of roughly €20 billion ($22.4 billion) for fiscal 2027, up from the €16.353 billion it booked in fiscal 2026, assuming a EUR/USD exchange rate of 1.15. The company expects a segment result margin in the mid-20s percent band, up from the 19.7% it recorded for fiscal 2026.

Infineon's earlier forecast covered AI data center power solutions only, at €2.5 billion, according to Bloomberg. The new figure combines those solutions with traditional data centers, which generate about €500 million a year.

JPMorgan $JPM analysts had expected fiscal 2027 data center revenue of between €3.5 billion and €4 billion, according to Bloomberg.

"Supported by an ongoing cyclical recovery and strong demand in our structural growth areas, we expect a significant increase in revenue and profitability in fiscal year 2027," CEO Jochen Hanebeck said in a statement. He cited electromobility, software-defined vehicles, energy infrastructure and semiconductor solutions for data center power supplies as key contributors.

Fourth-quarter revenue was €4.706 billion, with a segment result of €1.119 billion and a margin of 23.8%. Fiscal 2026 revenue rose 12% from a year earlier. For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Infineon expects revenue of about €4.6 billion and a segment result margin of about 23%.

For fiscal 2027, the company is guiding to an adjusted gross margin between the mid- and high-40s in percentage terms, and it has earmarked €3.0 billion to €3.5 billion for investment. It forecast adjusted free cash flow of about €2.2 billion and free cash flow of about €1.8 billion.

The main investment areas are production equipment at the Dresden facility in Germany, capacity for silicon carbide in Malaysia and gallium nitride output using 300-millimeter wafers in Villach, Austria, according to Bloomberg.

Infineon's management board intends to propose a dividend of €0.38 a share, up €0.03, at the annual general meeting in February 2027. Infineon stock rose 3.3% to €50.23 in Frankfurt trading on Tuesday morning.

#5549. Solana Validator Admission Ticket: Who Fell Short After Alpenglow, and How Marinade Responded

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

StakeThat +MEV went into one of Solana's first Alpenglow epochs with about 137,000 SOL staked with it and 0.8169 SOL in its vote account. The new admission ticket required 0.8198 SOL. It was 0.003 SOL short.

That's the first post-activation picture of Solana's Validator Admission Ticket. Most stake made it through without trouble, but a small group of validators keeps dropping in and out, often by amounts smaller than a typical transaction fee. At least one large stake program changed its delegation code hours before activation so its stake wouldn't stay with those validators. Marinade's published validator snapshots for epochs 1063 to 1067 show who fell short and what happened next.

According to Solana's BLS Pubkey and VAT page, Alpenglow has been active on mainnet since epoch 1064, which began around 13:36 UTC on October 21. From then on, each validator's vote account pays a 0.8 SOL Validator Admission Ticket at the start of every epoch. The fee is burned, and it pays for the following epoch. The first charge, at the start of epoch 1064, covered epoch 1065.

The rules are strict. If the fee can't be paid, Solana's page says, "your validator does not vote or produce blocks in the next epoch." Validators without a registered BLS key, or outside the top 2,000 by stake, are also excluded. Delegators to an excluded validator earn no inflation rewards for that epoch. The page also stresses that the balance "has to stay funded, not be funded once."

The vote account also has to stay above its rent-exempt minimum. In Marinade's data, the full requirement works out to 0.8197612 SOL.

Marinade publishes the inputs to its stake auction every epoch in a public pipeline repository. The input data checks whether each validator's vote account holds enough to cover the next epoch's ticket. Each snapshot covers about 670 validators and roughly 438 million SOL of stake.

Before activation, in the epoch 1063 snapshot, 33 validators holding 7.63 million SOL, or 1.74% of stake, were below the ticket balance. Once Alpenglow went live, that number fell quickly: 15 validators with 1.55 million SOL (0.35%) in epoch 1064, then 19 with 1.15 million (0.26%) in epoch 1065, the first epoch the ticket actually paid for. By epoch 1066 it was 13 validators with 790,000 SOL (0.18%), and by epoch 1067 just 8 with 710,000 SOL (0.16%).

The epoch 1063 count matches a figure in Marinade's own code history. A commit on October 21 notes that its new gate "refuses the 33 validators with vat_eligible false" in the 1063 snapshot.

The biggest pre-activation gaps were fixed in time. An unnamed validator with 2.05 million SOL of stake, Temporal Emerald with 1.23 million and Bitget Wallet with 593,000 were all below the ticket balance in epoch 1063. All three had topped up by the next snapshot. Of the 33 flagged before activation, 25 had recovered by epoch 1064.

So the fee didn't remove a large share of stake. The balance check affected less than 2% of stake at its peak, and about 0.16% by epoch 1067.

The validators that did fall short show a pattern: many of them nearly had enough.

Because the ticket is charged every epoch, a validator that tops up just enough to pass once will fail again an epoch later unless it adds more. Between epochs 1064 and 1067, between 3 and 11 validators fell below the threshold each epoch, while a similar number recovered.

The shortfalls also cut across setups. Every validator flagged in epoch 1067 runs either Agave 4.3.x, the client release the migration required, or the latest Firedancer build. Software readiness wasn't the issue. Keeping the balance funded was.

Solana offers a fix: routing block revenue to the vote account through solana vote-update-commission-collector. That keeps the account funded automatically, though the change takes two epochs to apply.

The bigger story is how stake programs reacted. Marinade, one of Solana's largest delegation programs, changed its auction code in pull request #153, merged at about 06:47 UTC on October 21, roughly seven hours before Alpenglow activated.

The change adds a new disqualifying condition, vatIneligible. A validator whose vat_eligible flag is false "gets no SAM and no backstop stake," because "Agave then pays its stakers no inflation rewards for the epoch." A null value never disqualifies a validator. The check currently tests only the SIMD-0357 balance, not BLS key registration.

The first version applied the rule only in Alpenglow epochs. Marinade's developers then caught a timing problem. Agave starts charging the ticket at the 1063-to-1064 boundary, and "a stake move made in epoch E takes effect in E+1," so the original rule "left Marinade stake on refused validators for epochs 1064 and 1065." The merged version refuses ineligible validators in every epoch.

The snapshots confirm it worked. In the epoch 1064 snapshot, 192,762 SOL of Marinade stake sat on ineligible validators, nearly all of it on one unnamed validator. By epoch 1065, that had dropped to 2,407 SOL, and by epoch 1066 to 10 SOL. A later commit gives the rule its own label and call to action in Marinade's interface, so operators can see why they've been excluded.

Marinade, in short, turned a protocol fee into a delegation rule of its own. A validator that misses one ticket loses an epoch of rewards, and it also loses Marinade stake until its balance recovers.

Before activation, Solana Compass reported that a community tracker flagged 45% of stake as not ready two days ahead of epoch 1064, mostly validators on Agave 4.3.0 and 4.3.1. The following day, that had dropped to 20.3%.

Marinade's snapshots show the software gap closing much as those warnings suggested it needed to. Stake on Agave 4.3.0 and 4.3.1 fell from 6.56% in epoch 1063 to 0.08% by epoch 1067. Firedancer operators, who had to switch to Agave for the migration, dropped from 11.0% of stake to 5.9% in epoch 1064. They then came back strongly, reaching 17.2% by epoch 1067, well above their pre-migration share.

The large readiness gap was about software and keys, and it was mostly closed by the time it mattered. The fee gap was always small.

For most delegators, nothing changed: more than 99.8% of stake sits with validators that keep their tickets paid. For those delegated to the few that don't, the cost is clear: no inflation rewards for that epoch, and in Marinade's case, stake moved elsewhere.

The protocol sets one requirement: 0.8 SOL in the vote account every epoch. Stake programs are now adding their own rules on top, starting with Marinade's. Validators that keep running near the threshold will keep losing epochs of rewards, and possibly delegations, until they keep a buffer or automate funding.

#5548. Lumbra gets $25M in backing to help intelligence community deploy reliable AI agents

When it comes to matters of national security, it’s vitally important to ensure that the right intelligence gets to the right decision-makers, but doing this in today’s complex information technology environments is challenging, to say the least.

Enter the artificial intelligence startup Lumbra Inc., which has just raised $25 million in early-stage A funding to develop specialist autonomous agents tasked with sorting through the most sensitive data of all. Today’s Series A round was led by Point72 Ventures and Ansa Capital, with participation from seed round investor Costanoa.

Lumbra was founded last year by former Central Intelligence Agency officer Aaron Brown and ex-special forces infantry officer Michael Hiebert. Together, they’ve built a platform called LumbraOS, which is designed to orchestrate AI agents within high-consequence and ultra-secure computing environments, where risks of any kind simply cannot be tolerated.

Brown explained that LumbraOS was built from the ground up as a “model-neutral platform” that allows operators to mix and match various proprietary and open-weight AI models, assigning them different national security- and intelligence-related tasks. The platform is built on three key pillars: Nebula, StarChart and Astrolabe.

Nebula is the component tasked with managing agent orchestration, and works by tracing every “claim” generated by AI agents back to the primary source data behind that claim, so that domain experts can validate their outputs before decisions are made. StarChart is a dynamic knowledge graph that links disparate insights across multiple datasets through embedded sensitivity tags. Meanwhile, Astrolabe enforces governance policies and continuously evaluates each agent after benchmarking their performance prior to deployment to monitor for any alarming behavior.

Traditional AI systems developers struggle for years to ensure they meet the most rigorous federal security standards, but Brown and Hiebert say they developed LumbraOS specifically for classified computing environments. Just two months after launching their platform, they quietly landed a multimillion-dollar contract with an unnamed U.S. intelligence agency, with their AI agents operating on a top-secret defense network within just six months.

Impressed with the startup’s technology, the Pentagon followed up by naming Lumbra as one of two companies that underpins its Agent Network project, and one of seven “pace-setting projects” within its broader AI Acceleration strategy.

Following this traction, Lumbra’s co-founders believe there is potential for LumbraOS to expand beyond the intelligence community. They’re targeting enterprises in high-stakes industries such as healthcare, finance and law, where sensitive data leaks are deal breakers.

Brown said most organizations in these industries only use autonomous agents for singular tasks, if at all. That’s because they lack the tools to make those agents controllable, transparent and reliable enough at large scale. With its traceable audit logs and strict governance controls, Lumbra thinks it can help organizations to deploy agents safely across their networks to automate more complex workloads.

“The organizations that get agents right will spend less time telling them what to do and more time deciding what they may touch and what their work must prove,” Brown said. “Thousands of agents working a question together can find an insight while there’s still time to act on it. Lumbra exists to give decision-makers an advantage at the moment of decision.”

To target the enterprise, Lumbra plans to use the funds from today’s round to expand its engineering and product development teams and accelerate its go-to-market operations.

Ansa Capital Managing Partner Marco DeMeireles said the problem of trust and verifiability is the biggest barrier to adoption for AI agents in high-stakes environments. “Lumbra has demonstrated its ability to bring these capabilities into production across some of the most demanding environments within the U.S. government,” he said. “We believe these same capabilities will become foundational to how the world’s most critical enterprises deploy AI.”

#5547. Polymarket's annualized revenue has topped $1.8 billion

Free daily briefing on global business news.

The prediction market's annual revenue run rate was above $1 billion in June, after it opened its U.S. exchange

Thomas Fuller / SOPA Images / LightRocket / Getty Images

Polymarket told CNBC on Tuesday that its annualized revenue has surpassed $1.8 billion, up from a run rate above $1 billion in June.

The growth is coming from Polymarket's U.S. exchange, a standalone marketplace that runs independently of the company's international DeFi platform, according to CNBC. In October, the domestic exchange processed notional volume of more than $14.5 billion, compared with $4 billion in June, according to CNBC, which cited TickerTracker data.

CNBC credited the jump in volume to high-traffic events such as the summer's FIFA World Cup and the NFL season kickoff in September. Combo event contracts, which operate much like sportsbook parlays that bundle several legs together, made up over 70% of the platform's trading activity on Sunday, according to CNBC.

Polymarket has started raising $1 billion in new funding, a round that puts its valuation at $21 billion, according to CNBC.

Polymarket had said in June that its annualized revenue had surpassed $1 billion, six weeks after its U.S. exchange opened to the public. Access widened in mid-May when the company removed the waitlist for mobile app users. The U.S. exchange had been in a restricted period since its December debut.

The company faces regulatory and political questions, according to CNBC. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is running a wide-ranging investigation of Polymarket, examining its advertising practices and whether it breached an earlier settlement requiring it to keep U.S. residents off its international exchange.

Polymarket could also draw heavier scrutiny under a Democratic Congress, in part because Donald Trump Jr., the son of President Donald Trump, advises the company, according to CNBC.

A Polymarket spokesperson told CNBC the company intends to cooperate with legislators while they get up to speed on the prediction market industry. "We welcome scrutiny," the spokesperson said.

#5545. Blackstone will buy a 15.57% stake in Indian lender IIFL Finance for about $532 million

Free daily briefing on global business news.

The investment is expected to lift IIFL's capital adequacy ratio to about 30% from roughly 17% on a pro forma basis as of September

Blackstone is set to buy 15.57% of Indian shadow lender IIFL Finance in a deal worth roughly 50 billion rupees ($532 million), according to Bloomberg.

The investment will be routed via Singapore-based Ingot SG Pte. Ltd., which is set to take roughly 83.1 million preference shares that are compulsorily convertible, priced at 602 rupees each, according to Bloomberg. Every preference share will convert into IIFL Finance equity at a one-for-one ratio.

IIFL Finance stock ended Monday's session at 627 rupees, roughly 4% over Blackstone's entry price. The stock is up roughly 3% so far in the current year.

Under the fundraising, IIFL founder Nirmal Jain will take up 15 million warrants valued at 9.03 billion rupees, according to Bloomberg. Co-founder R. Venkataraman will take up 4.5 million warrants, valued at 2.71 billion rupees. Ardent Impex Private Ltd., an entity of the founder group, will take 1.5 million warrants valued at 903 million rupees.

Jain and Mukesh Mehta, chief investment officer of Blackstone India Private Equity, said in a statement the deal will shore up the lender's finances and back its growth, according to Bloomberg. The expansion includes technology spending as well as co-lending tie-ups with banks. Blackstone said it intends to partner with IIFL's management team as the lender keeps expanding.

On a pro forma basis as of September, the capital infusion is expected to raise IIFL Finance's capital adequacy ratio from roughly 17% to about 30%, according to Bloomberg.

Bloomberg News reported back in September that Blackstone was one of several international investors weighing a stake in IIFL Finance. Fairfax Financial Holdings bought a 60.72% holding in IDBI Bank in October, paying 528.78 billion rupees, according to Bloomberg; as of the end of September, it owned about 13.6% of IIFL Finance.

Blackstone committed roughly 62 billion rupees last year in return for a stake of up to 9.99% in Federal Bank, according to Bloomberg. The firm also controls mortgage lender Aadhar Housing Finance.

IIFL Finance lends against gold and provides home loans, business loans, property-backed financing and credit for small and medium-sized enterprises. The lender runs upward of 4,900 branches spanning more than 500 Indian cities and manages roughly 1.15 trillion rupees in assets, according to Bloomberg.

#5543. PuppyGraph raises $10M to let AI agents query enterprise data as a graph

Graph query engine startup PuppyGraph said today it has raised $10 million in new funding to build out its enterprise go-to-market operation.

The round follows the general release of version 1.0 of its software. PuppyGraph provides a query engine that lets companies treat data already sitting in their warehouses and lakehouses as a single graph, without first moving it into a separate graph database. The company says artificial intelligence agents running on it can work across 3,000 enterprise tables and get graph query results back in under a second.

Agent projects tend to hit trouble once they leave the pilot stage, according to PuppyGraph. The company’s own example asks which critical systems an attacker could reach from a compromised account, a question that means tracing how identities and permissions connect across thousands of tables in several systems.

A proof of concept might cover 30 to 50. Teams that scale past that find schema descriptions alone eating into an agent’s context window, and PuppyGraph said queries running several relationships deep can stall until they time out.

Data teams setting up PuppyGraph 1.0 start from a schema that an AI-assisted tool drafts out of their existing tables. Once they have approved it, users can put questions to the graph in plain English.

PuppyGraph has its own agent for that, and the Model Context Protocol lets companies bring in the AI tools they already use. Agents are kept from guessing how the data fits together. Any agent that references a relationship nobody set up gets its query bounced, and the error that comes back is written for the agent to act on.

When PuppyGraph connects to Snowflake Inc. or Databricks Inc. it can obtain short-lived credentials tied to the user’s identity, so nobody has to hand over long-lived keys. Row-level permissions configured on the data still apply, and the company says it checks them at each hop of a traversal.

“The insights of enterprise data will soon be generated by agents,” said Weimo Liu (pictured), co-founder and chief executive of PuppyGraph. “Users will expect to ask questions that cross departments and systems, beyond the workflows someone built into a dashboard.”

PuppyGraph’s customer list includes Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Palo Alto Networks Inc., and the announcement also named Coinbase Global Inc., Datadog Inc. and Trend Micro Inc. as customers. Xinyu Liu, a staff software engineer at Coinbase, said that because the exchange connects straight to tables it already keeps in Snowflake and Databricks, “standing up a new graph is a schema definition, not a data migration.” Weimo Liu worked as a software engineer at Google LLC before co-founding the Santa Clara-based company.

PuppyGraph’s annual recurring revenue grew sevenfold over the past year, by the startup’s count. No dollar figure was disclosed.

Particle Future and defy.vc led the Series A round. It is the second time defy.vc has led a round for PuppyGraph, after a $5 million seed round in November 2024. PuppyGraph will also put some of the new money into engineering.

Amy Yin, a partner at defy.vc, said writing a query is now a job a user can hand to Anthropic PBC’s Claude. Executing it across billions of relationships still “takes serious engineering,” in her view.

Developers can download a free version of PuppyGraph with a single Docker command and no sign-up form, and the company says it takes about 10 minutes to go from deployment to a first query. Investors have now put $15 million into the startup.

#5542. Trump says Iran war could end "fairly soon" after Qatar talks, plays down new strikes

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Oil prices slid on Tuesday as the president called new U.S. strikes on Iran "quite unlikely," though Iran disputes that talks are under way

President Donald Trump said on Monday the conflict with Iran might end "fairly soon," following his White House meeting with Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani.

"We're seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it's going to be ending fairly soon," Trump told reporters. He said Tehran was "talking very politely" with Washington.

Trump described new U.S. strikes on Iran as "quite unlikely," though he said the U.S. could resume them if circumstances change. He repeated that Tehran will never be permitted to obtain nuclear arms.

In a Truth Social post, Trump said Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Kuwait "prefer the status quo," which includes the naval blockade of Iran, according to CNBC.

Al Thani said he was "grateful for the positive discussions on reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region," according to Bloomberg. Bloomberg, citing an unnamed official, said negotiations are expected to continue and military escalation is unlikely while they do.

Large gaps remain. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on Sunday that the talks "hadn't been very productive" because of Iranian demands, according to Bloomberg. Tehran is demanding that the U.S. end its blockade of Iranian Persian Gulf ports and drop sanctions before any negotiations begin. Washington wants Iran to halt its strikes on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz and to give ground on its nuclear work.

Iran has sent the U.S. a proposal through Qatari intermediaries under which the Strait of Hormuz could reopen within two days, in exchange for sanctions relief and a different shipping lane through the strait, according to CNBC. Washington was reviewing it, CNBC said. Iranian officials dispute that talks are under way. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said Washington should stop “manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks,” according to CNBC.

Oil prices fell after Trump suggested the conflict might wrap up soon. Brent crude for January delivery was down 2.7% at $90.14 at 5:33 a.m. ET on Tuesday, a level not seen since August. U.S. West Texas Intermediate was down 2.4% at $84.78.

The U.S. and Israel began the war with strikes on Iran. A truce followed in early April, and the two sides agreed in mid-June to a memorandum of understanding that included a ceasefire. It collapsed about two weeks later, according to Bloomberg.

Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, according to Bloomberg, and Vice President JD Vance named the war as the main reason.

#5539. Breach Secure Now Launches MCP Connector, Putting Security Program Data to Work in ChatGPT, Claude and Microsoft Copilot

New connector helps MSPs prioritize client needs, create customized reports and demonstrate service value, while giving business leaders and employees greater visibility into security progress.

MORRISTOWN, N.J., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Breach Secure Now (BSN), a provider of cybersecurity, AI awareness, productivity and compliance solutions delivered to small and midsize businesses (SMBs) through Managed Service Providers (MSPs), today announced the Breach Secure Now MCP, a new integration that brings BSN Portal Data directly into ChatGPT, Claude and Microsoft.

MSPs manage valuable security program data across their clients' portfolios, but finding the right information often means navigating multiple dashboards, pulling individual reports, and spending time organizing results. The Breach Secure Now MCP changes this process by allowing users to ask questions about their data in plain language, directly within familiar AI assistants.

The connector extends beyond MSP administrators, giving their clients business leaders and employees access to information appropriate to their BSN account permissions. MSPs can prioritize client needs and prepare for business reviews, leadership teams can evaluate security program performance, and employees can track their own security awareness progress.

Helping MSPs Turn Program Data into Action

For MSPs, the Breach Secure Now MCP provides a practical and highly impactful way to review security program data across their managed clients, identify accounts that need attention, prioritize outreach and prepare for Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs).

Rather than reviewing individual client reports, MSPs can ask questions such as, "Which of my clients I call first, and why?"  The AI assistant can quickly retrieve and analyze available BSN Portal Data, helping partners identify priorities and turn information that previously required extensive manual reporting into useful summaries in minutes. MSPs can also generate customized client reports that bring together relevant security program information metrics, helping them demonstrate going value and have more productive client conversations.

"MSPs have a tremendous amount of valuable information available through the security programs they manage, but turning that information into meaningful client conversations takes time," said Art Gross, CEO of Breach Secure Now. "With the Breach Secure Now MCP, we're continuing our commitment to first-to-market innovation by making it easier for partners to understand where their clients need attention, show the progress they're making, and have more productive conversations about security. Just as importantly, we're giving business leaders and employees a way to better understand their own results."

Greater Visibility for Business Leaders and Employees

The benefits extend beyond MSP administrators to the organizations and employees they support.

Business leaders can use their AI assistants to review their organization's training participation, Employee Secure Score and aggregate phishing results. They can summarize program performance for leadership, identify areas that need attention, and determine where additional follow-up may be needed.

Employees can use their AI assistants to check their Employee Secure Score, review completed training and access their personal phishing history. They can also see how their score has changed over the past six weeks, giving them a clearer picture of their security awareness progress and where they may need to focus their attention.

Chris Gross, Sr AI Product Director, adds, "For years, partners have asked us for more flexibility in how they access and present their security program data," said Chris Gross, Senior Director of AI Product at Breach Secure Now. "With the Breach Secure Now MCP, they're no longer limited to predefined reports. They can ask their own questions, create tailored summaries, and use their AI assistants to build reports around what matters most to their clients. This opens up a whole new way for MSPs to put their data to work."

Secure, Role-Based Access to BSN Portal Data

The Breach Secure Now MCP uses Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard that enables AI assistants to connect securely with applications and data sources.

Users sign in with their existing BSN credentials, and access is limited to the information permitted by their BSN account role. MSP administrators can view data for their managed clients, client management can access organizational information, and employees can view their personal results.

The connector is read-only and does not change records within the BSN Portal.

"We're meeting our partners where they already work. BSN's MCP server brings portal data into everyday AI tools, so partners, company managers, and individual users can get the answers relevant to their role just by asking," said AL Lowenstein, CTO of Breach Secure Now.

Available Now, with Additional Capabilities Planned

The Breach Secure Now MCP is available now to BSN users with the appropriate account permissions and supports ChatGPT, Claude and Microsoft Copilot.

Development is already underway to expand the BSN Portal Data and reporting capabilities available through the connector, with additional enhancements planned for future releases.

The same connection will also support the upcoming BSN Skills Libraryâ¢, planned for Q1 2027. Building on BSN's commitment to employee education, the Skills Library will provide guided AI workflows built on proven frameworks, helping employees develop practical skills and apply AI across a wide range of business functions.

Free daily briefing on global business news.

The Hong Kong exchange has cleared Alibaba to proceed; the size and structure of the offering have not been finalized

Alibaba Group Holding announced in an exchange filing on Tuesday that T-Head, its in-house chip design unit, has applied to list in Hong Kong, advancing a planned spin-off, according to Bloomberg.

Alibaba said the Hong Kong bourse has given it approval to go ahead, and T-Head filed its listing application on Sept. 11. The offering's scale and format remain undecided.

T-Head is fully held by Alibaba and, according to the filing, is expected to stay within the group as a subsidiary once it is listed. Alibaba characterized the unit as a supplier of data-center chips spanning the full technology stack, which power computing systems at the system level for customers in China.

Alibaba said the spin-off would give investors a way to price T-Head on its own, apart from the wider group. It also could draw in investors who want a pure-play stake in the chip business, the company said.

A standalone listing would let T-Head turn directly to capital markets for both equity and debt, Alibaba said. The company said it would also make it easier for the unit to obtain loans from banks.

The filing follows a series of chip announcements from Alibaba. The company unveiled a new AI chip, the Zhenwu V900, in September at its annual Apsara Conference in Hangzhou. CEO Eddie Wu said the chip delivers three times the performance of the previous Zhenwu M890, with mass production and commercial release targeted for the first quarter of 2027.

Alibaba released the Zhenwu M890 in May, and its Zhenwu chips were already in use by more than 650 customers across sectors including automotive, finance, energy and manufacturing. The company has committed to spending more than $53 billion over three years on cloud and AI infrastructure.

U.S. export controls that cut off Chinese companies from Nvidia $NVDA's top-tier chips have accelerated efforts by firms such as Alibaba to build their own semiconductor capabilities.

#5537. Adobe expands AI assistant into creative workflows

Adobe Inc. today announced an expansion of its CX Enterprise Coworker agentic artificial intelligence platform into its GenStudio content supply chain platform.

The company said the integration move allows creative professionals to bring AI agents into production workflows to develop, manage and deliver personalized marketing content at large scale.

The announcement, made at its Adobe MAX conference in Miami, extends CX Enterprise Coworker beyond its initial focus on customer analytics and marketing into content planning, creation and distribution. The technology provides a conversational interface for coordinating AI agents across Adobe applications and third-party systems.

Adobe said it’s aiming to reduce the manual work involved in producing marketing campaigns while maintaining human oversight and brand consistency. It’s also introducing several new capabilities across its GenStudio portfolio, including AI-assisted campaign planning, automated brand compliance, reusable creative workflows and expanded 3D product visualization.

Central to the initiative is Adobe Brand Intelligence, a machine learning system that captures an organization’s brand standards, including the unwritten practices and preferences that traditionally have resided inside employees’ heads.

“As we move to a world where creatives are directing agents, the context that’s locked in the hearts and minds of creatives is made available to agents so they can start to produce content that is on brand,” said Varun Parmar, Adobe’s senior vice president of GenStudio and Firefly for Enterprise.

Brand Intelligence will be integrated into Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign and Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise. New intelligent asset adaptation capabilities can automatically resize and rearrange campaign designs for different media formats while preserving brand standards.

The system also incorporates continuous learning to keep guidelines current as creative practices evolve.

“It’s ingesting reviews, approvals and rejections by the creatives,” Parmar said. “Based on that information, it’s able to infer the latest guidelines.”

Administrators can inspect and override those conclusions to prevent outdated or incorrect practices from becoming embedded in automated workflows.

Another addition is Ideation Space, a collaborative AI-powered canvas within Adobe Workfront. It combines historical campaign performance, audience information and other enterprise data to help marketers develop campaign briefs.

In a demonstration, Adobe showed how Coworker could retrieve project assignments, research audience characteristics, coordinate with an AI copywriting agent and evaluate proposed designs using synthetic audience simulations. The platform can also be used to run surveys of human respondents.

Adobe is extending Firefly Graph for Enterprise with a feature called Capsules that packages complex creative workflows into simplified applications that other employees can run without mastering the underlying tools. Another feature, Node Publishing, allows teams to share reusable workflow components.

New 3D Digital Twin capabilities enable enterprises to modify product imagery, materials, lighting and camera angles and generate animations without repeatedly photographing physical products.

CX Enterprise Coworker supports external applications and custom-built systems through the Model Context Protocol, enabling enterprises to connect their existing technology investments.

Adobe emphasized that the expansion isn’t intended to give AI agents unrestricted authority over creative decisions. “CX Enterprise Coworker enables human-led agent-accelerated work,” Parmar said. “At every step when the agent is making a decision, it’s coming back to the human and asking.”

Early deployments have accelerated audience definition, traditionally a time-consuming part of campaign development, according to Adobe, although executives provided no quantitative productivity figures. The company expects similar improvements in content production.

The new GenStudio integrations are being made available today, with some Firefly Graph capabilities remaining in beta test. Adobe said the expanded Coworker functionality won’t require additional charges for customers with existing subscriptions.

#5536. Cosmos Hub Approves Gaia v29 With 99.41% Support Ahead of October 28th Upgrade

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Proposal #1059 passed with 49.59% turnout as the chain counts down now to block 33,618,500 on October 28th, where validators are told to run the security-patched v29.0.1 binary, not the version named in the proposal.

The Cosmos Hub's latest upgrade drew almost no opposition. About 168.5 million ATOM voted on Proposal #1059, and only 2,335 ATOM voted No. Under that one-sided result is an unusual change: the Hub's stakers voted to remove the governance route that earlier generations of Cosmos proposals used to change the chain's own settings.

Proposal #1059 schedules the upgrade of the Cosmos Hub to Gaia v29.0.0. It finished voting on October 27 at 12:00 UTC with a PASSED result. The vote approves the upgrade, but the software has not run yet. The chain still has to reach the upgrade height, halt, and restart on the new binary. Until that happens, Gaia v29 is approved but not yet live.

On-chain records show 49.59% of staked ATOM voted, against a 40% quorum requirement. Yes took 99.41% of the vote, or 167,514,965 ATOM. No With Veto took 0.58% (982,855 ATOM), Abstain took 0.01% (14,360 ATOM), and No rounds to 0.00% (2,335 ATOM).

The veto share is the main number to watch in a Cosmos governance vote, because a large enough veto rejects a proposal even if Yes wins. At 0.58%, the veto bloc was far too small to matter. That fits the proposal's nature. It is a maintenance release that removes deprecated code and updates dependencies, and it has no economic or political stakes.

The forum discussion covered one governance point: a delegator's own vote overrides their validator's vote. A few large validators did not decide the result on their own. Delegators could have overridden them, and very few chose to vote differently.

The proposal names v29.0.0, but operators are not supposed to run that build at the upgrade height. On October 23, three days into voting, the Gaia team tagged v29.0.1 and updated the official forum post to recommend it.

The patch changes only one thing: it rebuilds Gaia with Go 1.26.10 instead of Go 1.26.7. That picks up the Go security fix tracked as CVE-2026-111943 (GO-2026-6809). The project's upgrade notes call v29.0.1 a non-state-breaking patch release, so it computes the same chain state as v29.0.0. Nodes that already installed v29.0.0 can switch at any time by replacing the binary and restarting.

Operators using Cosmovisor need to know one detail. The on-chain upgrade name stays v29.0.0, so the v29.0.1 binary still goes into the upgrades/v29.0.0/bin/ directory. If a validator names the folder after the patch version, Cosmovisor will not find the binary when the chain halts. The project's sample service configuration has automatic binary download turned off, which means each operator has to put the correct binary in place before the halt.

Gaia v29 removes the x/params module from the Cosmos Hub. That module is the original, centralized store for parameters, and it backed the legacy ParameterChangeProposal governance route. The release changelog lists the change under API-breaking changes: "The legacy ParameterChangeProposal governance route and cosmos.params.v1beta1.Query service are no longer available."

In practice, governance has already moved on. Each module now owns its parameters, and changes go through that module's own governance message. The legacy route remained as a fallback, and v29 removes it. The rate-limiting module was the last part of the Hub still wired to the old params subspace. In v29 it no longer depends on it.

The forum Q&A states who is affected. RPC providers, wallets, explorers, and governance dashboards should check whether they still call the params v1beta1 query service or create legacy parameter-change proposals. After the upgrade, those calls will fail on the Hub. For most users nothing changes. The proposal requires no token migration, and balances, delegations, and IBC assets are unaffected.

The second API-breaking item affects multisig accounts specifically. Gaia v29 moves the Hub from Cosmos SDK v0.53.4 to v0.53.8, and the changelog warns: "As of cosmos-sdk v0.53.8, --gas auto gas simulation is broken for multisig senders. Multisig transactions must specify a fixed --gas value until this is fixed upstream."

This matters in practice. The Hub's weekly update of October 22 said the problem applies to the Community Pool migration multisig. That multisig is handling a USDC.n migration spend that was moving toward an on-chain proposal during the same week. Treasury signers, custody desks, and DAO operators who build transactions with --gas auto will need to set gas by hand until the upstream SDK is fixed.

The same release also brings CometBFT from 0.38.23 to 0.38.25, the IBC rate-limiting middleware from 10.1.0 to 10.7.0, and runc from 1.2.8 to 1.3.6. It also moves the build toolchain from Go 1.25 to Go 1.26.

The upgrade handler, the code that runs once at the upgrade height, does more cleanup than the proposal summary describes. It first deletes everything in the deprecated provider store, the state left over from the Hub's time as an Interchain Security provider. Next it wipes the legacy x/params store. Last, it removes a receipt left behind by the earlier v28.3.1 balance migration.

The code also shows how cautious the Gaia team is about the upgrade. The stores stay mounted, and their contents are cleared as ordinary state changes. Unmounting them entirely could cause version-mismatch errors when nodes load the chain from disk. Gaia v29 has also run on the Hub's provider testnet since October 13, about two weeks before mainnet.

At 15:32 UTC on October 27, Mintscan showed block 33,618,500 as "not yet created". The chain was at block 33,604,199, with 14,301 blocks to go. At the recent average block time of 5.722 seconds, the Mintscan countdown for block 33,618,500 estimated the height for about 14:16 UTC on October 28. The forum's original estimate was 13:50 UTC. The real time depends on how fast blocks are produced over the next day.

When the chain reaches that height, block production stops. It restarts only after validators holding more than two-thirds of voting power are back online on the new binary. That makes the vote result only half the story. The other half is whether validators show up on v29.0.1 promptly, so that the halt lasts minutes rather than hours.

#5535. Wise expands US product suite, giving customers new ways to earn returns

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Wise, the global technology company building the best way to move and manage the world's money, today announced an expansion of its US product offering, giving people and businesses two new ways to earn a return on the money they hold with Wise.

The expansion introduces Wise Interest and Stocks, two new products available directly from customers' existing USD balance. Unlike traditional alternatives that require customers to move or lock away their money to earn a return, customers who opt in to these products keep instant access to their funds,1 meaning they can continue to send and spend from the same balance with no withdrawal penalties. Wise Interest and Stocks are offered by Wise US Assets Inc.2, a registered broker-dealer. Member of SIPC, which protects securities customers of its members up to $500,000 (including $250,000 for claims for cash). Explanatory brochure available upon request or at www.sipc.org.

Vinay Nilakantan, Head of Product for North America at Wise, said: "People and businesses around the world are keeping more money with Wise than ever. Global customer holdings grew 40% to $39 billion last financial year alone.3 Now, we want to offer Wise customers more ways to put that money to work, without compromising the convenience and flexibility they expect from us.

"In the US, earning a competitive return too often means locking your money away or juggling multiple accounts. But with Wise Interest and Stocks, people and businesses in the US no longer have to choose between making their money work harder and actually being able to use it. They have the freedom to do both."

Introducing new ways for Wise customers to earn a returnWise Interest allows customers to earn a return on USD held with Wise through a money market fund holding government-backed assets. Customers' money remains instantly available to send and spend within the same balance, offering greater convenience and flexibility.4 Returns, which are not guaranteed, are calculated daily and paid into customers' accounts monthly, and over 90% of returns earned may also be exempt from state and local income taxes.5

For customers looking for potential longer-term returns, Stocks gives people and businesses a simple way to invest money held with Wise in an S&P 500 index fund.6, 7 This lets them invest across a diverse range of leading US companies while keeping a high degree of liquidity. Investing involves risk, including possible loss of principal. Wise Interest seeks to preserve the value of an investment, but the investment value of Stocks will change with the market.

Customers can start using either product directly from their existing USD balances by simply selecting Wise Interest or Stocks. In line with Wise's commitment to transparency and low costs, customers will see the fees associated with each product clearly before opting in.

Expanding Wise's existing US product suiteThe launch comes as customers increasingly use Wise to hold more of their money and look for more ways to grow those funds. Income earned by US customers through Wise's existing Basic Interest offering, which allows customers in the US to receive interest on USD, GBP and EUR, increased by almost 17% year over year in FY26.8 Basic Interest is an opt-in feature that allows customers to earn interest on eligible balances held in a Wise account with Wise US Inc. Customer funds are held at Wise US Inc.'s program bank, which pays interest on those funds, and a portion of that interest is passed through to eligible customers.9

Wise Interest and Stocks build on the range of existing products already available to Wise personal and business customers in the US. Today, customers can hold and convert more than 40 currencies, get paid in nine currencies using local account details, send money internationally with 77% of payments arriving instantly (in under 20 seconds),10 and spend around the world with the Wise Multi-Currency Card.

The launch of Wise Interest and Stocks marks the first time Wise has operationalized its US broker-dealer license, which it holds in all 50 states, to offer more tailored products to local customers.

#5533. Anthropic targets an IPO valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, less than expected

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Investors were expecting roughly $1.5 trillion a week ago, but several large backers pressed for a lower number after AI stocks sold off

Anthropic launched the roadshow for its initial public offering on Tuesday, setting an expected price range of $70 to $78 a share for 825 million shares of Class A common stock.

Anthropic is selling 801,351,354 of those shares, and certain existing stockholders are selling the other 23,648,646. Anthropic will receive no proceeds from the stockholders' sales. The company also expects to give underwriters a 30-day option to buy up to 123,750,000 additional shares.

At the top of the range, Anthropic could carry a fully diluted valuation as high as $1.405 trillion, and the offering could raise as much as $64.35 billion before costs, according to CNBC. Anthropic is targeting a valuation near $1.33 trillion, and an offering priced at the midpoint would bring in upwards of $61 billion, according to The Wall Street Journal. CNN puts the midpoint valuation at about $1.1 trillion once options and unvested stock are counted.

Anthropic has applied to list its Class A stock on the Nasdaq $NDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT." A registration statement has been filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and must become effective before any stock can be sold. Copies of the preliminary prospectus are available from Goldman Sachs $GS and Morgan Stanley $MS. Trading could begin as soon as next week, according to CNN.

Anthropic has agreed to sell $26 billion of Class N common stock in a private placement to Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom $AVGO, Google $GOOGL, Micron $MU, Microsoft $MSFT, Nvidia $NVDA and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company at the IPO price, according to CNBC. Those shares will be unregistered and exempt from underwriter lock-up agreements.

In an amended filing, the company said sales through the first three quarters, ending Sept. 30, came to $33.24 billion, a jump of about 1,200% from a year earlier. It posted a net loss of $104 billion over that span, mostly from fair-value adjustments on its derivative liabilities and its convertible notes. Run-rate revenue stood at roughly $81 billion as of late October, an increase of $10 billion over the month before.

The valuation target is well below earlier expectations. Investors were expecting roughly $1.5 trillion a week ago, but several large backers pressed for a lower number after AI stocks sold off sharply last Thursday, according to The Wall Street Journal. A figure near $2 trillion was under discussion several months back.

#5532. Tessera Unveils Integrated LADAR- Based Perimeter Security Solution Combining AI Platform with Thermal Imaging and Intelligent Classification

Integrated solution pairs DFSL's laser-based LADAR sensors with Zorronet's LYBA AI command-and-control platform to detect, visually verify and classify events at short range, without RF radar emissions

NETANYA, Israel, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tessera Defense and Homeland Security Inc. (NYSE American: HLSQ) ("Tessera" or the "Company") today announced the commercial launch of its integrated perimeter security solution that combines LADAR (laser detection and ranging) sensors from DFSL with Zorronet's command-and-control platform, powered by its LYBA AI core. DFSL and Zorronet are independent subsidiaries of Tessera.

The modular solution integrates precision LADAR-based optical detection with commercially available day/night and thermal PTZ cameras, supported by AI analytics. It is designed for detection ranges of approximately 30, 60 and 100 meters, targeting sites that need accurate short-range detection and classification, particularly where RF-based radar is restricted, unsuitable or undesirable.

Conventional perimeter systems detect movement and raise an alert, leaving operators to interpret each event. Tessera's solution is designed to take the next steps automatically.

When a DFSL LADAR sensor detects an object, it passes the object's location to LYBA, which can automatically point a compatible PTZ camera at the target. LYBA then applies computer vision and AI analytics to verify, classify and analyze the event, giving operators context rather than a bare motion alert.

Depending on the AI models selected and the imagery available, the system can be configured to:

The goal is to turn raw detection data into actionable operational intelligence that supports faster, better-informed security decisions.

Rather than a fixed set of detection rules, LYBA offers a library of existing AI models and operational scenarios, built to grow as customer requirements evolve. Organizations can select relevant scenarios, integrate compatible third-party and open-source models, and develop or fine-tune models for specialized applications.

For example, a customer can configure the system not only to detect a person entering a restricted area, but also to determine whether that person is accompanied by an animal, is carrying a potentially suspicious object, or is exhibiting a predefined behavior of interest. New or adapted models are validated through a controlled integration process before they are deployed.

The solution supports secure on-premises and isolated (air-gapped) deployments, so approved AI capabilities can run without continuous internet connectivity. Software and model updates are delivered through controlled maintenance procedures, allowing the system to evolve without replacing the underlying sensing and imaging hardware. This approach is intended to meet the cybersecurity and operational requirements of sensitive facilities while providing long-term technological flexibility.

Short-Range Detection Without RF Radar Emissions

Unlike radar, which transmits radio-frequency energy, DFSL's LADAR uses laser-based optical sensing to detect and locate objects, so the detection process itself requires no RF radar transmissions. This can be an important advantage at facilities where radar emissions are restricted, where RF-sensitive equipment is present, or where operators want to minimize additional RF transmissions. Associated communications equipment can be configured with wired connectivity to meet applicable site restrictions.

The solution is built around a camera-agnostic architecture that supports compatible, commercially available motorized PTZ cameras, including day/night and thermal models, rather than requiring proprietary imaging hardware from a single manufacturer.

DFSL's LADAR provides precise location and detection data, the camera provides visual observation and tracking, and LYBA fuses both into a single operational picture. Configurations can be tailored to coverage requirements, environmental conditions and applications, and new analytics and AI capabilities can be added over time without redesigning the detection infrastructure.

Part of Tessera's Integrated Security Strategy

"The challenge in modern security is no longer simply detecting movement. It is understanding what is happening, how significant it is, and how to respond," said Michael Oster, Chief Executive Officer of Tessera. "By combining DFSL's precision LADAR with Zorronet's AI capabilities, we are bringing complementary technologies together into a new generation of intelligent security solutions. What sets this approach apart is its flexibility: customers can select scenarios, add models and adapt the system as their requirements evolve, including in isolated and highly sensitive environments. This is Tessera's strategy in practice: turning advanced technologies into practical, scalable solutions for real-world security challenges."

About Tessera Defense and Homeland Security Inc. (Formerly BiomX Inc.)

Tessera Defense and Homeland Security Inc. (NYSE American: HLSQ) is a physical security technology company providing integrated, bespoke security solutions that connect detection, intelligence and response across complex security environments. The Tessera platform integrates cameras, sensors, detection technologies, AI and other security infrastructure to identify threats, understand events and coordinate response in real time. Tessera provides the technology, hardware and implementation expertise needed to tailor security solutions to the specific requirements of each site, helping customers deploy and optimize integrated security systems across critical infrastructure, energy, digital infrastructure and homeland security applications. For more information please visit https://tesserainc.ai/.

#5531. Cowbell unveils AI liability insurance for small businesses that deploy AI agents

Cyber insurance provider Cowbell Cyber Inc. today unveiled Cowbell AI Liability Insurance, a standalone policy for U.S. small and midsized businesses that covers losses caused by the artificial intelligence agents they deploy.

The new policy is meant to deal with a problem that arises when businesses let agents move money or change customer records with nobody signing off first. Coverage hinges on a trigger the company calls an “AI Incident.” The definition takes in model drift and attacks that manipulate an agent, not just software acting without approval.

Cowbell describes an accounts payable agent misreading approval statuses and paying a supplier twice with no human check. Part of that money disappears when the supplier goes into liquidation.

Unrecovered funds like those can be covered, and the policy also pays to investigate what happened and take the agent offline. Inaccurate or unsafe output can be corrected or withdrawn at the insurer’s expense, with recipients notified.

Usage charges an agent racks up without authorization are covered too, such as when a loop goes unchecked. Cowbell also covers LLMjacking, where an outsider uses stolen credentials or application programming interface keys to run AI workloads and leaves the business holding the bill.

Claims brought by customers fall on the third-party side. Cowbell’s example there is a bookkeeping firm whose agent files client tax returns using outdated rates, and the clients sue once the penalties and interest arrive.

In a case like that, the policy can pay defense costs and any damages or settlements, and the same goes for suits alleging algorithmic discrimination or bodily injury caused by reliance on AI output. Regulatory proceedings are also covered, and where the law allows it so are certain fines and penalties.

Cowbell Chief Commercial Officer Simon Hughes said AI liability is “no longer only about people using AI,” pointing to agents that act with no human in the decision-making chain. When one goes rogue, he said, a business can take its own losses and face customer claims at the same time. Hughes said the policy was written with that double exposure in mind.

Underwriting draws partly on three AI-specific Cowbell Factors covering observability, autonomy and governance. They show underwriters how closely a business monitors its AI tools and how much authority those tools have to act on their own.

Cowbell’s Risk Advisor agent, launched in October, uses the factors to explain risk signals to policyholders. Businesses can see their own scores by connecting Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT and other tools through Cowbell Connectors.

Cowbell already sells some AI coverage. Prime One, which it launched in April for U.S. companies with $250 million to $1 billion in annual revenue, includes affirmative coverage for AI-related incidents inside a cyber policy. The new product is sold on its own and aimed at smaller businesses.

Cowbell AI Liability Insurance goes on sale Jan. 1, 2027, and will be available only through wholesale brokers on a non-admitted basis. Cowbell is a venture capital-backed company that has raised more than $200 million, including a $60 million Series C round from Zurich Insurance Group Ltd. in July 2024.
